title: Ἵππος καὶ στρατιώτης
part: The Horse and the Soldier (Chambry 142 · Perry 320)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 142 (= Perry 320). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« », [ ] for words Chambry deletes as interpolated). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ἵππον τὸν ἑαυτοῦ στρατιώτης, ἕως μὲν καιρὸς τοῦ πολέμου ἦν, ἐκρίθιζεν, ἔχων συνεργὸν ἐν ταῖς ἀνάγκαις.
sentences.tr: Hippon ton heautou stratiōtēs, heōs men kairos tou polemou ēn, ekrithizen, echōn synergon en tais anankais.
sentences.l: A soldier, so long as the season of war lasted, fed his own horse on barley, having him as a fellow-worker in times of need.
sentences.n: κριθίζω is formed straight off κριθή, barley: "to feed on barley", the good grain — set against the ἄχυρον of the next line. ἕως with the imperfect indicative measures the whole stretch of time, and the μέν here waits for the δέ that opens the following sentence. συνεργός is one who works alongside you, not a servant.

sentences.t: Ὅτε δὲ ὁ πόλεμος κατέπαυσεν, εἰς δουλείας τινὰς καὶ φόρτους βαρεῖς ὁ ἵππος ὑπούργει, ἀχύρῳ μόνῳ τρεφόμενος.
sentences.tr: Hote de ho polemos katepausen, eis douleias tinas kai phortous bareis ho hippos hypourgei, achyrōi monōi trephomenos.
sentences.l: But when the war ceased, the horse did service for certain servile tasks and heavy loads, being fed on chaff alone.
sentences.i: But when the war stopped, the horse was put to drudgery and heavy loads, and fed on nothing but chaff.
sentences.n: ἄχυρον is chaff, the husk left after threshing — the poorest feed there is, and the exact opposite of the barley above. δουλεία is the condition of a slave and so the work of one; ὑπουργέω εἰς is to render service towards a thing. τρεφόμενος, present passive participle, is the state he was kept in throughout.

sentences.t: Ὡς δὲ πάλιν πόλεμος ἠκούσθη καὶ ἡ σάλπιγξ ἐφώνει, τὸν ἵππον χαλινώσας ὁ δεσπότης καὶ αὐτὸς καθοπλισθεὶς ἐπέβη.
sentences.tr: Hōs de palin polemos ēkousthē kai hē salpinx ephōnei, ton hippon chalinōsas ho despotēs kai autos kathoplistheis epebē.
sentences.l: But when war was heard of again and the trumpet was sounding, the master, having bridled the horse and having armed himself as well, mounted.
sentences.n: ὡς here is temporal, "when". ἠκούσθη is aorist passive with πόλεμος for its subject: war itself "was heard", the Greek way of saying that word of it went round. καὶ αὐτός is "he too, for his own part" — the master arms as well as the horse.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ συνεχῶς κατέπιπτε μηδὲν ἰσχύων· ἔφη δὲ τῷ δεσπότῃ· « Ἄπελθε μετὰ τῶν πεζῶν [τῶν] ὁπλιτῶν ἄρτι· σὺ γὰρ ἀφ’ ἵππου εἰς ὄνον με μετεποίησας, καὶ πῶς πάλιν ἐξ ὄνου ἵππον θέλεις ἔχειν ; »
sentences.tr: Ho de synechōs katepipte mēden ischyōn· ephē de tōi despotēi· « Apelthe meta tōn pezōn [tōn] hoplitōn arti· sy gar aph’ hippou eis onon me metepoiēsas, kai pōs palin ex onou hippon theleis echein ; »
sentences.l: But he kept falling down again and again, having strength in nothing; and he said to his master: « Go off now with the heavy-armed men on foot; for you made me over from a horse into a donkey, and how do you wish to have a horse again out of a donkey? »
sentences.i: But the horse kept collapsing, with no strength left in him, and he said to his master: « Off with you now, and march with the heavy-armed foot; for you made me over from a horse into a donkey, and how do you expect to get a horse back out of a donkey? »
sentences.n: Chambry brackets [τῶν] as a later insertion he would delete — the phrase reads the same without it. μηδέν is an internal accusative with ἰσχύων, "having strength in no respect". μεταποιέω is to make a thing over into something else, and ἀπό … εἰς marks what it was made from and into. ὁπλῖται are the heavy-armed infantry: the horse is telling his rider to go and be a foot-soldier.

sentences.t: Ὅτι ἐν καιρῷ ἀδείας καὶ ἀνέσεως τῶν συμφορῶν οὐ δεῖ ἐπιλανθάνεσθαι.
sentences.tr: Hoti en kairōi adeias kai aneseōs tōn symphorōn ou dei epilanthanesthai.
sentences.l: That in a time of security and relaxation one must not forget misfortunes.
sentences.i: The story shows that in a time of security and ease one must not forget misfortunes.
sentences.n: A moral in the bare Ὅτι form: the introducing verb is unexpressed in the Greek, which begins simply "That…", and is supplied in the idiomatic line. ἐπιλανθάνομαι takes the genitive of what is forgotten (τῶν συμφορῶν). ἄδεια is the state of having nothing to fear and ἄνεσις the slackening of a strain — between them they name the peacetime in which the soldier stopped buying barley.
